decision:
STANDS as a scope and status record, under ruling M-D67-1, with read status COMPARED-BY-M. The journal text itself was not read here.

WHICH REPORTS THE EVIDENCE SUPPORTS.
(a) The audit's OPEN was right when it was written on 2026-09-26. The tree then said "NAMED-NOT-READ ... MUST NOT be quoted as errors in the journal version until it is read". The audit's own what_would_change_the_grade said that if the journal prints the same (2.16), (3.7), (3.8) and "Delta > 1" as v1, the entry becomes STANDS as a scope record.
(b) Two commits on 2026-09-27 (138153f and dbb3c9c) then changed the tree. M compared the two versions and reports "Both are exactly the same". M also ruled M-D67-1: an arXiv paper that M confirms is the same as the journal paper carries the journal paper's weight. M's comparison asserts exactly the condition the audit named. Under M-D67-1 that comparison is now the operative standard.
(c) Verifier 2 (re-run the re-derivation) is correct on three points: the audit's reverify command fails against today's tree, its "no drift" claim is stale, and so are its line citations. I reproduced the failure. The copied script exits 1. All B and A checks pass, and so do T1, T4 and T6. T2, T3 and T5 fail only because the clause was rewritten and docket67-raw/ was added.
(d) Verifiers 1 and 3 READ the APS abstract page, and I re-READ it this pass. It gives "Received 9 December 1992", "Published 15 May 1993", Vol. 47, Iss. 10. The full text is "AUTHORIZATION REQUIRED". The abstract is identical to the v1 abstract: difflib finds 198 words in each and zero differences.
All three verifiers proposed OPEN, on the tree as the audit described it. Verifier 2 explicitly left open whether M-D67-1 lifts the grade, calling that a question for M's ruling. M has now ruled, and this adjudication applies the ruling.

THE GRADE EVIDENCE.
(1) The tree's statement about PRD 47, 4510 (fluctuation.py:150-155) is exact.
- JOURNAL_VERSION_READ = False is true: the APS full text is still behind authorization.
- M's words are held verbatim (fluctuation.py:168-171 matches the ruling text exactly).
- The carry to the journal is attributed to M's comparison, "not on this file's reading".
- ledger.py raises an error if the docstring and the flags disagree (:1046-1049 and :1307-1308).
- fluctuation.py --selftest exits 0, and so does ledger.py --selftest.

(2) The v1 content that carries is READ and re-derived.
- This pass I re-read v1 at source through alphaXiv: (2.15)-(2.16), (3.7), (3.8) and the claim after it, (3.18), (3.19), the Fig. 1-2 captions (gamma = delta = 0, theta = pi/2, "Otherwise, Delta ~ 1"), the Sec. III.B sentence "By the point that the state is sufficiently squeezed to have rho<0, we always have that Delta is at least of order unity", and Sec. V.
- The audit's checks A1-A11 pass on re-run. The final line of (2.16) is half its middle line. (3.7) is off by a factor 1/(1+eps^2). At the witness point the exact Delta is 0.5134 against 2.0118 from printed (3.8). z3 proves that rho<0 implies 1/3 < Delta < 1.
- I checked the case (ii) counterexample without using fluctuation.py, with my own Gaussian generating-function moments and a numeric Fock check at N=400 (run/kfprd_check2.py). On the curve theta = pi/2, gamma = delta = 0, |alpha|^2 = (1-e^{-2r})/8, write S = sinh r and C = cosh r. Then <:T00^2:> - rho^2 = 3(S^2 - C^2 + 1) = 0 identically, while rho/K = S(S - C) < 0. At r = 1, rho = -0.4323 K and the numeric Delta is 2e-14.
- On the same curve, KF's printed (3.18)/(3.19) give Delta = 0.9920, 0.9976 and 0.9999 at r = 0.5, 1 and 2.
- So the tree's KF_QUALITATIVE_CONCLUSION_SURVIVES = False and its KF_FIG2 HYPOTHESIS numbers both reproduce.

(3) One point does not need M's comparison. The headline sentence, "We find in all cases studied that the energy density fluctuations are large whenever the local energy density is negative", is READ in the journal's own abstract. The case (ii) computation refutes it. That KF's cases include the displaced squeezed family D(alpha)S(zeta)|0> is READ in v1 Sec. III.B. It carries to the journal body only on M's comparison, though the journal abstract does name "squeezed states".

(4) No measured datum enters the results the tree uses, so no moved datum can move the conclusion.

NAMED HYPOTHESIS H-M. The text of PRD 47, 4510-4519 is the v1 text, including its equation numbering, as M reports. Nothing here can check this against the journal body.
- What can be checked agrees with it: the title, authors, affiliation and abstract are identical; 15 May 1993 matches M's "May of 1993"; and v1's date line "February 1993" matches M's "written in February 1993".
- One fact runs the other way and is recorded: the journal records "Received 9 December 1992", earlier than v1's date. So v1 is plausibly the revised, post-referee manuscript. That fits it being the accepted text, but it is not a reading of the printed text.
- If H-M failed, only the carry to the journal would fall. The v1 findings, which are READ and computed, would not.

Nothing here favours M beyond what is computed. The v1 discrepancies are graded under their own gr-qc/9304008 keys. This entry grades the journal-version record, and that record is accurate as the tree now stands.

The sites are fluctuation.py:150-155, 164-171, 188, 370-371 and 558-563; ledger.py:1042-1054, 1281-1320 and 3576-3577; LEDGER.md:183; and specthm.py:906-908. The grade covers four things:

- M's words are held verbatim;
- the v1 discrepancies and the refuted qualitative conclusion carry to the journal under M-D67-1, on M's comparison;
- the selftest and the ledger enforce agreement between the docstring and the flags.

DOES NOT COVER:
(i) A READ of the journal body. STANDS rests on the named hypothesis H-M (journal text = v1 text, on M's comparison), as M-D67-1 permits.
(ii) The individual v1 grades. Each is graded under its own gr-qc/9304008 key: (2.16), (3.7)-(3.8), the claim after (3.8) (WRONG), the qualitative conclusion, (3.18)-(3.23), (3.41)-(3.43), (3.45), the quartic renormalisation (NARROWED) and the measure (NARROWED). This entry only carries them.
(iii) Whether the journal's equation numbers match v1's. That is inside H-M.
(iv) Whether an erratum exists. The APS abstract page shows no erratum link, which is weak evidence and not proof.
(v) Whether Fig. 2 was computed from the misprinted (3.19). The tree holds this as a HYPOTHESIS, and so does this entry.

M-D67-1 is applied only to this pair (gr-qc/9304008 v1 and PRD 47, 4510), which M confirmed.

The tree now records KF_QUALITATIVE_CONCLUSION_SURVIVES = False, with a computed counterexample in KF's own case (ii). I reproduced it independently: Delta = 0 identically, with rho = K sinh r (sinh r - cosh r) < 0, on theta = pi/2, gamma = delta = 0, |alpha|^2 = (1-e^{-2r})/8. later_literature should add Hu & Phillips, gr-qc/0004006, as 'contested'. I READ it this pass. It cites the journal as refs [4] and [10], misspelled 'C.-I. Kou'. It calls KF's criterion a 'fallacy' because Delta = 2/5 in the Minkowski vacuum (point-split along time) and in hot flat space, which corroborates the tree's thermal Delta = 2/5. It lists KF's states as vacuum+2, squeezed vacuum and Casimir, omitting the displaced squeezed family. It restates no journal equation.

Correction to verifier 1: Hu & Phillips' '0 <= Delta <= 1 always' assumes a positive-definite, un-normal-ordered variance. KF's normal-ordered <:T00^2:> - rho^2 need not be positive, which is why KF's (3.2) carries an absolute value. So Hu & Phillips is not an independent confirmation of the bound rho<0 => Delta<1. That bound rests on the z3 computation alone.
